subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 24-year-old woman undergoes preconception carrier screening because her brother has an autosomal recessive disorder. A single nucleotide variant is identified in the third position of a codon, and the encoded amino acid is predicted to remain unchanged. The laboratory classifies the variant as a benign silent polymorphism.
question: Which property of the genetic code best explains why this variant does not alter the protein?

options.text: The code is unambiguous, meaning that each codon specifies only one amino acid.
The code is universal and conserved throughout evolution.
The code is read as a continuous sequence without punctuation (commaless).
The code is read from a fixed starting point without overlap.
The code is degenerate (redundant), and the third nucleotide of a codon can vary (wobble).

explanation_correct: Most amino acids are encoded by more than one codon, which makes the code degenerate or redundant. The first two nucleotides of a codon are essential for anticodon recognition, whereas the third can vary (the wobble hypothesis), so many third-position substitutions are silent. Methionine (AUG) and tryptophan (UGG) are the exceptions, each encoded by a single codon.

explanation_incorrect.A: Unambiguity means a codon never specifies more than one amino acid; it does not explain why different codons can encode the same amino acid.
explanation_incorrect.B: Universality means the code is nearly the same across species, with mitochondria as the main exception; it does not explain tolerance of third-position changes.
explanation_incorrect.C: Being commaless means the sequence is read continuously without spacer nucleotides, with some viruses as exceptions.
explanation_incorrect.D: A fixed, nonoverlapping reading frame describes how the sequence is read and does not account for synonymous codons.

educationalObjective: Degeneracy of the genetic code, together with third-position wobble, allows many single-nucleotide substitutions in the third codon position to be silent.
